risks.basis: THIS FILE has a confirmed defect on record
risks.risk: sairnlaw.html saveTime() wrote rate:Number($('ttrate').value)||0, so a blank, unparseable or missing hourly rate became ZERO with no complaint at either end -- `rate` appeared in no validator anywhere in api/. saveInvoice() computes the invoice total as hours x rate, so a billable hour stored at rate 0 adds $0.00 to the bill while rendering in the billing table as an ordinary billable hour: the work is on the record and the fee is not, and nothing downstream reports it. Same shape as the codeless-hour defect one field over and arguably worse, since a codeless hour at least shows '--' in the code column. Fixed by refusing a BILLABLE entry whose rate is not a finite number above zero, in api/_lib/law-timeentry.js and in the browser path; a no-charge entry is left alone because rate 0 is what no-charge MEANS, and an absent `billable` field is read as no-charge exactly as every reader in the app reads it. THE SAME COMMIT also removed a second, non-behavioural defect recorded on its own open-work row: the module justified itself -- in its header, its REQUIREMENT line and the user-facing refusal NO_CODE_MESSAGE -- on a LEDES export that does not exist in this app. NOT closed: `hours` is still unchecked at the server and hours 0 produces the identical $0.00 line.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnlaw) has this defect on record
risks.risk: api/sd-data.js law_timeentries write branch: a time entry was upserted with whatever billing_code arrived, including an empty string or no field at all. sairnlaw.html's saveTime() writes the select value unchecked, and billing_code appeared in NO server validator -- zero hits across api/sd-data.js and api/_lib/*.js -- so the entire law_ write branch validated one thing for twenty-odd resources: that a payload has an id. A codeless billable hour renders as a normal billable hour with an empty column, on the record saveInvoice() computes an invoice total from. The app file described this defect in its own comment above LAW_BILLING_CODES; the 2026-09-09 fix made the code list a constant so the select cannot render empty, which closed the CAUSE and left the gate unbuilt. Fixed by api/_lib/law-timeentry.js, presence and shape only, wired into the write branch before the upsert.

risks.basis: the same app (sairnlaw) has this defect on record
risks.risk: sairnlaw.html saveInvoice() marked every time entry on a new invoice invoiced=true and wrote the list back with st('law_timeentries', teList) -- localStorage -- while making exactly ONE network write, the invoice itself. The flag that says these hours have been billed never reached the server, so its copy of every billed row still read invoiced:false. Because lawHydrateAll() merges additively and never overwrites a locally-held id, a workstation with no copy yet hydrates those hours FRESH as unbilled, rInvoiceEntryPicker() filters on billable && !invoiced and offers them again, and nothing says they were already sent to the client: the same hours can be invoiced twice. Fixed by writing each touched entry back whole (sd-data.js upserts data:payload wholesale, so a patch would lose hours, rate and billing_code) and by NAMING a write that did not land -- a legacy row with no billing_code is refused by api/_lib/law-timeentry.js, so this can genuinely fail on real data. NOT closed: a device that already holds the entries keeps its stale invoiced:false.
